title: Low System Pressure
shortDescription: Hydronic loop pressure has fallen below the minimum threshold.
fullDescription:
Buderus Logamatic GB142 and SSB units display 2P when the integrated pressure transducer reads below ~7 psi (0.5 bar). The boiler will not fire to protect the heat exchanger.

Low pressure on a sealed system points to either a leak, a waterlogged expansion tank, or normal early-life venting of dissolved gases. Refill via the manual fill valve to 12-15 psi cold and observe.
safetyWarning: Do not over-pressurize; the relief valve will discharge above 30 psi.

causes.cause: Slow leak in piping or radiator vent

fixSteps.title: Refill to spec
fixSteps.instruction: Open the fill valve until the gauge reads 12-15 psi (0.8-1 bar) cold.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Check radiator vents, circulator flanges, relief valve discharge.

fixSteps.title: Test expansion tank
fixSteps.instruction: Tap the tank; a hollow sound is good, dull/heavy is waterlogged.

whenToCallPro: If pressure drops repeatedly within days — there is a leak that needs locating.

faq.q: How often should I add water?
faq.a: Almost never on a sealed system — repeated refills mean a leak.

title: High System Pressure
shortDescription: Loop pressure is above the maximum allowed.
fullDescription: 3P appears when the pressure transducer reads above ~30 psi (2.5 bar). Most often this is a failed pressure-reducing/auto-fill valve that is letting house water continuously feed the loop, or a waterlogged expansion tank that cannot accept thermal expansion.
safetyWarning: Excessive pressure will trigger relief-valve discharge — keep clear of hot water.

fixSteps.title: Isolate auto-fill
fixSteps.instruction: Close the cold-feed valve to the boiler temporarily.

fixSteps.title: Bleed to 1 bar
fixSteps.instruction: Open a low-point drain to reduce pressure to 12-15 psi.

fixSteps.title: Tank check
fixSteps.instruction: Verify expansion-tank air precharge with a gauge while system is depressurized.

whenToCallPro: If the auto-fill or expansion tank needs replacement.

faq.q: Why does pressure climb only when hot?

title: Supply Sensor Open
shortDescription: Boiler outlet temperature sensor is open-circuit.
fullDescription:
4Y means the supply (heat-exchanger outlet) NTC reads open. The control disables firing because it cannot enforce limit protection.

Most often a connector worked loose during service or the sensor cable was pinched when the cover was reinstalled.
safetyWarning: Power off before disconnecting sensor leads.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; reseat the supply sensor harness at the BC10/BC25.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm at room temp; should be near 12kΩ on Buderus NTC. Replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Sensor well replacement requires draining the boiler.

faq.a: Use the OEM Buderus part to match the temperature curve.

title: Ignition Failure
shortDescription: Burner failed to establish flame after ignition retries.
fullDescription: 6A is the Buderus ignition lockout. After three failed ignition attempts the GB142/SSB locks out and waits for manual reset. Causes mirror other condensing boilers: low gas, fouled electrode, blocked condensate, or a failed gas valve.
safetyWarning: If you smell gas evacuate and call your gas emergency line.

fixSteps.title: Verify gas
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm gas is on at the boiler valve.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Press Reset and observe ignition.

fixSteps.title: Clean electrode
fixSteps.instruction: If recurring, clean and gap the ignition assembly.

whenToCallPro: Gas valve or pressure work requires a licensed gas tech.

faq.a: Two; if it returns the third time, stop.

title: Flame Lost During Run
shortDescription: Established flame disappeared during a heat call.
fullDescription: 6C is logged when the unit ignites successfully but loses flame during the burn. Common reasons are a failing flame rod losing rectification, momentary low gas pressure, or condensate blocking the flue.
safetyWarning: Repeated mid-run flame loss can produce unburned gas — investigate before resetting again.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame rod
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, pull and lightly polish the flame rod.

fixSteps.title: Inspect flue
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the vent looking for sags pooling condensate.

faq.a: No — 6C is purely a flame-supervision event.

title: Gas Valve Drive Fault
fullDescription: 6L is a safety lockout from the control's gas-valve supervision circuit. Possible causes are a shorted gas valve coil, a damaged harness, or a failed control board.
safetyWarning: Treat as a serious gas-valve fault and isolate gas.

fixSteps.title: Isolate gas
fixSteps.instruction: Close the manual gas valve on the boiler inlet.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Have a tech ohm the gas valve coil and inspect the board.

whenToCallPro: Always — this is gas-valve supervision lockout.

faq.q: Can a power surge cause this?
faq.a: Yes; surges damage the FETs that drive the gas valve coil.

title: Pressure Switch / APS Open
shortDescription: Air pressure switch did not close after fan start.
fullDescription: 9B indicates the inducer ran up to speed but the air-proving switch never closed. Either the fan is not actually moving air or the switch/hose is faulty.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass — this protects against vent obstruction and CO spillage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Clear any blockage; verify in winter for ice/snow.

fixSteps.title: Test hose
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the pressure-switch hose for cracks or condensate.

faq.a: Not directly — the switch prevented operation. Always have a working CO alarm.

title: High Limit Trip
fullDescription: 9H means the manual or auto high limit opened. Hydronic causes: air-bound HX, dead pump, closed isolation valve. The control will lock out until reset.
safetyWarning: Investigate the flow problem before resetting.

fixSteps.title: Bleed
fixSteps.instruction: Vent the boiler and high points of the loop.

fixSteps.title: Verify flow
fixSteps.instruction: Touch supply piping during a call — should warm quickly with circulator on.

faq.q: Why right after a power outage?
faq.a: Air enters the system; bleed thoroughly.

title: Fan Feedback Out of Range
shortDescription: Combustion blower RPM does not match command.
fullDescription: A1 is reported when the fan tach signal and the PWM command disagree by more than the allowed tolerance. Worn brushes, debris fouling, or a bad PWM cable are usual.
safetyWarning: Disconnect line voltage at the cabinet before fan work.

fixSteps.title: Inspect impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove inlet, vacuum any debris.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the fan harness on both ends.

faq.q: What is the typical fan life?

title: Frost Protection Active
fullDescription:
Not strictly an error — CY is an informational code shown when the GB142/SSB has activated its built-in frost protection. The boiler runs the pump and may briefly fire to keep the heat exchanger above 5 °C.

Homeowners frequently report this in summer when an unconditioned mechanical room cools quickly overnight.
safetyWarning: Not a safety event — but ensure the boiler has gas and electricity available year-round.

fixSteps.title: Verify room temperature
fixSteps.instruction: If the boiler room is below 50 °F, add heat or insulation.

fixSteps.title: Confirm settings
fixSteps.instruction: Check that frost-protect parameters match installer guide.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot find a setting causing nuisance display.

faq.a: No — it prevents freeze damage to the boiler.
